C01.why: The Exit 8 anomaly loop is proven on Steam and is already proven on Roblox (Sell Fries! ~112K peak, licensed Exit 8 with 8-player co-op), so this is mostly assembled from current Roblox hits, not extracted from an indie. Exit 8's tension comes from one person looking closely and alone. With 4 friends spotting together on a small phone screen, that tension gets diluted, and spotting subtle changes is harder on mobile.
C01.fix: Adopt the real differentiator from I'm on Observation Duty / Exit 8: split the camera feeds so each player sees different cameras, and require a second player to confirm an anomaly before reporting it. Make anomalies large and readable at phone size (an object appears, moves or changes colour, nothing at pixel level).

C02.why: The source is strongly proven: Keep Talking is a classic, and BOMBANANA had 675K+ demo players and was #1 at June Next Fest. The cyclic info chain is a real principle extraction, and there is no known Roblox rival. But both sources run on frantic verbal description. Squeezing the Book role through an 8-icon wheel risks slow, frustrating rounds with matched strangers, and the mandatory 3 players adds friction to filling lobbies.
C02.fix: Design every module so the manual is purely pictographic and each rule can be answered by pointing and stamping (colour, shape, count), never by describing. Paper-prototype this with players who cannot talk before building anything. Make 2-player the default mode and 3-player the advanced mode.

C03.why: This has the strongest direct transfer evidence on the panel: the crude Roblox Fart Together copy reached 13M+ visits and ~14K peak before it was taken down. RV There Yet? (~100K CCU) also validates the shared vehicle. A one-button hold thruster is ideal for mobile and needs no voice. It is close to a reskin of Fart Together, though, and loses the toilet-humour hook that drove its virality. Fast-follow clones are likely.
C03.fix: Replace the fart joke with a kid-safe comedic propulsion gimmick that has personality (sneezing walruses, shaken soda bottles, leaf blowers with recoil gags). Make vehicle thruster layouts the depth layer, with each vehicle a new coordination puzzle. Ship fast and make the server the only physics owner so the raft does not jitter.

C04.why: Inspect-and-spot-the-fake is a well-proven mechanic: Papers, Please, which is also mobile-proven, and Probably Stolen (660K+ demo players, ~40K CCU). Flipping the player from fraudster to detective is genuine principle extraction rather than a clone, tap-and-drag tools fit touch well, and there is no known Roblox competitor. The weaknesses: the source is a solo game, so the co-op split feels bolted on, and comparing items against a catalogue may be too reading-heavy for younger players.
C04.fix: Make every tell purely visual (wrong colour stamp, missing UV glow, odd weight icon) and never textual. Hand each tool to a different player so co-op is mandatory. Make Forger Night the headline multiplayer mode, since hidden-role bluffing is what gives the solo source social replay.

C05.why: This is the best kid reframe on the panel. No Body No Problem!'s physics-evidence stealth becomes 'hide the mess before Mom checks', and it builds on Granny-style 1vN, which Roblox audiences already love. The mechanic needs no voice because hiding is physical. The source is unproven commercially, though (Next Fest top 5, no figures, unreleased). Networked physics clutter with 6 players and a precise grab on touch are real porting risks.
C05.fix: Track evidence as about 30–50 discrete server-authoritative objects and decals with clear states (clean/hidden/exposed) instead of free physics debris. Use auto-grab-nearest on mobile. Make the Parent's inspect deterministic so finds feel fair.

C06.why: The source is weakly proven (Find the Needle had an ~8.6K demo peak and is unreleased). The server-wide shared pile is an original and social adaptation. But the inner loop is a standard Roblox tycoon/incremental in a falling simulator market, and 'whoever's machine finds the needle' is a lottery that will feel unfair to small or new players.
C06.fix: Tie needle odds to each player's share of contribution and reward every contributor when any needle drops. Make the automation spatial and visible (conveyors that actually carry hay to the pile) so it reads as Find the Needle and not as another tycoon.

C07.why: PEAK and Chained Together are massively proven, but the 2024 wave already flooded Roblox with chained obbies and SUMMIT exists. PEAK's charm depends heavily on proximity voice and precise PC climbing, and snap-to-ledge on touch drops most of that. This is a clone, not an extracted principle.
C07.fix: Extract a different principle, such as a rope with asymmetric roles (one belayer who can only anchor and reel, one climber who can only move), or a rescue-descent framing, so it is not 'Chained Together obby #50'.

C08.why: Content Warning is proven (6M+ claims), but its comedy comes almost entirely from recorded voice reactions. Without voice, a montage of server-side event tags loses the core payoff. Ghost-hunting already exists on Roblox.
C08.fix: Record character CFrames, emotes and ragdoll states server-side during filming, then play them back as a real 3D replay in the theatre so the funny part becomes body flailing and emotes instead of voices. Add preset reaction buttons (scream, faint, run) that boost views.

C09.why: Swapping YAPYAP's voice-casting for rune drawing is a smart principle extraction (performative input survives), and gesture casting has precedent. But YAPYAP's fun is social shouting, not solo tracing. Drawing while moving with a thumbstick on a phone is awkward, and drawing with a mouse on PC is different again. The wave-defence wrapper sits in a crowded Roblox tower-defence space.
C09.fix: Remove simultaneous movement: players stand at tower posts and only draw. Keep traces local and ephemeral to stay clear of free-form drawing policy. Use 6–8 forgiving runes, and make cross-player combos the social payoff (show both players' runes merging on screen).

C10.why: The Mewgenics inheritance meta is proven (115K peak, 1M+ sales) and lands on Roblox's strongest native appetite: pets, hatching and mutations (see Grow a Garden mutations). That is genuine principle extraction, and tap/drag auto-battles suit mobile. The risk is that reducing Mewgenics's deep tactics to auto-battles leaves a generic pet TD with a family tree attached.
C10.fix: Keep one meaningful tactical decision per battle (placement plus one active ability). Make mutations visually dramatic and inheritable in readable ways, and let players show off the family tree in the lobby. Use 'fusion'/'family' framing throughout.

C11.why: This is a mashup of things Roblox already has at scale (DONT SPLASH ~116K peak, R.E.P.O. clones, liminal obbies). R.E.P.O.'s noise-hunting entity relies on proximity voice and microphone noise, which do not port. I see no extracted indie principle.
C11.fix: Take one unported idea, such as Big Walk's 'communication range is terrain' (pings and flares only carry within line of sight, and the entity is drawn to pings), so the no-voice limit becomes the mechanic.

C12.why: The role-split cockpit is proven, but Backseat Rally already brings it to Roblox (28–55K peak). 'The pilot can't see the gauges' is a Keep Talking-style voice dependency carried only by pings. IRON NEST's diegetic panel procedures are the more novel part and are underused here.
C12.fix: Build the game on IRON NEST-style multi-step physical procedures, where the engineer runs fixed lever/dial sequences that show as visible cockpit changes and the pilot reacts to the plane physically. Coordination then becomes reading each other's actions rather than relaying information through pings.

C13.why: OpenFront.io is a proven but divisive browser RTS, and this is a near-direct port, not a principle extraction. A 2D tap-drag map transfers well to mobile. Alliances and betrayal without chat, plus early snowballing, are rough for a young Roblox audience over 15 minutes.
C13.fix: Shorten matches to about 8 minutes and add team modes with structured alliance buttons (propose, accept, break). Add strong catch-up mechanics so eliminated or losing players aren't stuck spectating for 10 minutes.

C14.why: It combines proven parts well (Totally Reliable Delivery Service, R.E.P.O.'s value meter, Overcooked), and the floating value meter is a readable, voice-free signal. But driving plus a two-person physics carry is exactly where Roblox network ownership and touch controls struggle, and R.E.P.O.-style carry is already widely cloned.
C14.fix: Remove free driving (use a short auto-route with lane-switch taps) and focus the game on the hazard carry. Make co-carry server-owned with a shared 'balance' input, not real physics, so jitter can't destroy cargo unfairly.

C15.why: Merge Tactics is proven on mobile, a drag-and-drop shared-pool auto-battler is ideal for Roblox touch, and the genre is thin on Roblox. It is mostly Merge Tactics/TFT with an 8-player knockout, and Squad Busters shows that a fun core without meta depth churns fast. Auto-battler economy reading is also a hurdle for young players.
C15.fix: Give the onboarding a 3-toy 'merge' tutorial vs bots, and remove the economy (gold/interest). Add a persistent collection meta (earned toy unlocks that change the shared pool) so there is a reason to return beyond the match.

C16.why: 7 Days Cat-Sitting is already a Roblox game, and this version drops its actual hook (the anomaly horror twist), leaving generic Overcooked-style chores. Neither originality nor transfer value is added.
C16.fix: Either fold it into C01 as a chapter, or add one distinctive mechanic, such as each pet having a hidden 'personality rule' the team must deduce from behaviour.

C17.why: Tricky Towers is a solid but modest source, and turn-based co-op stacking leaves most players idle. Physics stacking on Roblox is non-deterministic across clients and frustrating when a tower collapses from network jitter. Stacking games already exist on Roblox.
C17.fix: Make placement simultaneous, with each player owning a crane and their own piece queue, and settle the tower only on the server. Add a versus sabotage card (wind gust, slippery piece) to create memorable moments.

C18.why: There is no proven game source (it cites a report concept, Tamagotchi and Twitch Plays). The core assumption, 'your server' raising a monster all week, conflicts with how Roblox works: servers are transient and players are matched into random instances.
C18.fix: Tie the monster to persistent teams or houses that players pick (4–6 factions) and store it in DataStores rather than to a server. Use MemoryStore for weekly cross-faction battles.

C19.why: Worst Class Ever is a strong source (#1 Oct Next Fest, ~300K demo players), and the flashlight-freeze plus shared Mischief meter combination is a fair extraction that suits mobile and needs no voice. But Roblox already has several NPC-blend games (Be NPC or Die, DISGUISE, In Plain Sight, Prank the Teacher), so differentiation is thin.
C19.fix: Make the flashlight beam the core mechanic: statues can only be tagged inside the beam and the Guard's battery is limited, which gives a readable Red Light Green Light rhythm that NPC-blend competitors lack. Use preset prank stations only (no free drawing).

C20.why: just volleyball is only a top-20 demo, and the tap-to-aim mechanic suits mobile. But Volleyball Legends already dominates Roblox volleyball with simplified controls, so this adds almost nothing.
C20.fix: Apply the one-touch-scales-from-1v1-to-team principle to an under-served sport or an invented one (dodgeball-tennis, sky-volley with jump pads) rather than going head-to-head with Volleyball Legends.

overall_notes: No concept reaches 8 on this criterion. The best adaptations (C03, C04, C05, C10) extract a principle and reframe it for kids without depending on voice. C03 has the only direct Roblox evidence: the Fart Together copy reached 13M visits before it was taken down. The recurring failure is sources whose fun lives in proximity voice (Content Warning, R.E.P.O., PEAK, Keep Talking). C02 and C08 must prove their no-voice replacement in a paper or graybox prototype before any production commitment. Clones of games already on Roblox (C07, C11, C16, C20) score low regardless of how strong the source is. Several Steam source numbers come from search summaries and aggregators, not primary pages, so source-strength judgments carry medium confidence.
